title: DevProof verification policy
description: Rules deciding whether verified facts about an immutable subject satisfy a caller's trust requirements. A policy is trusted configuration supplied by the caller; it is never read from the artifact being evaluated, because an attacker who controls a bundle must not control the rules it is judged by. Decoding is strict in both the loader and this schema: an unknown field is an error, since a rule this build does not understand is a rule it would not enforce, and silently ignoring one turns a strict policy into a permissive one (DP-014).

requireDigestReference.description: Reject a tag before anything is fetched. Digests are authoritative; tags are pointers (DP-007).

allowedFormats.description: Acceptable bundle format versions. Empty means any format this build supports.

signatureRules.description: Constraints on who signed. Threshold counting happens after cryptographic verification and identity matching.

threshold.description: How many distinct accepted identities are required. Zero with no identities means signatures are not required. Must not exceed the number of listed identities -- a threshold no evidence could ever satisfy is indistinguishable from a policy that is working.

requireTransparencyLog.description: Demand a proven transparency-log inclusion, not merely a timestamp.

identityRule.description: One accepted signer. Exactly one form may be given: a bare public key, or an OIDC identity. A rule naming both would be ambiguous about which had to match, and "either" is spelled by writing two rules.

identityByOIDC.description: An issuer is always required. A subject with no issuer would accept that subject from any issuer, which is trivially forgeable by standing up an issuer.

subject.description: OIDC subject, matched exactly. Mutually exclusive with subjectPattern.

subjectPattern.description: Regular expression alternative to subject, compiled at policy-load time and anchored at both ends by the evaluator. An unanchored pattern matching a substring is how an identity rule gets bypassed.

provenanceRules.description: Constraints on what the evidence says. These apply to provenance claims, not to payload identity: two attestations may truthfully describe different source histories for one subject, and policy chooses which history it is willing to trust.

required.description: Demand provenance evidence. Provenance that must be present must also be signed by somebody, so this implies a threshold of at least one.

predicateTypes.description: Acceptable predicate types. DevProof provenance is https://devproof.thingz.io/provenance/v1, which embeds a SLSA Provenance v1 document unchanged, so a policy requiring https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 is satisfied by the embedded document (DP-024).

requireLockDigest.description: Demand that provenance records a lock digest, which is what makes a build's inputs auditable after the fact.

allowedTypes.description: Permitted source types, such as git or path.

requireImmutableResolution.description: Demand that every source resolved to something immutable.

evidenceRules.description: How candidate evidence is treated. An OCI repository is an open attachment surface, so the presence of an unrelated or malicious referrer must not by itself make a valid subject unverifiable.

rejectInvalidMatchingEvidence.description: Make malformed evidence that claims a required type fatal on its own. Even when false, policy still fails if the remaining verified evidence cannot satisfy its requirements.

allowTagFallback.description: Permit evidence stored under the fallback tag scheme on registries without the referrers API. Off by default, because that mode cannot express a set and silently replaces (DP-028).

maxAge.description: Bound how old accepted evidence may be, as a Go duration such as "720h". Measured from an authenticated signing time against the evaluation clock; evidence carrying no authenticated time cannot satisfy the rule. Unset, or the empty string a Go decoder cannot distinguish from absent, means age is not considered.

limitValue.description: Zero means unset and inherits the effective default. Zero never means unlimited.

limits.description: Resource bounds. A policy may tighten a bound but never relax one: the effective value is the minimum across the client's limits, the request's limits, and these, which keeps a policy from being usable as a privilege escalation against the embedding application's own configuration (DP-021). Each maximum here is the format's hard ceiling from DP-020; a value above it is refused at load time.
